text: Hi Sam, your order #A-1042 shipped on November 12 and the estimated delivery date is November 21.
note: Facts match the ticket.

text: Our records show order #A-1077 was delivered. If you can't find it, check with neighbours or your building's front desk; carriers often leave parcels there.
note: UK. Verified status plus practical tip, no promise.

text: Order #A-1103 is still being processed and hasn't shipped yet. The current estimated delivery date is November 28.
note: Negation of shipped status, matching date.

text: I'm not able to approve refunds from this inbox. Refund requests go through the Returns page in your account, where the returns team reviews them under our published policy.
note: Mentions refund only to explain the process.

text: Your invoice is under My Orders > Order details > Download invoice.
note: Self-service instruction.

text: Thanks for letting us know it arrived. Enjoy!
note: Pure courtesy.

text: The total charged for order #A-1042 was $129.90.
note: Matching amount.

text: Estimated delivery dates come from the carrier and can change; the tracking link in your account shows the latest scan.
note: Explains uncertainty without committing.

text: I don't have any information about when that item will be restocked. Availability is updated on the product page.
note: Mentions restock without promising it.

text: To change the delivery address while an order is still being processed, go to My Orders > Edit address.
note: Self-service instruction.

text: Warranty terms are set by the manufacturer and listed on the product page. Support can't extend or change them.
note: Mentions warranty to decline changing it.

text: Sorry for the hassle this has caused.
note: Generic apology, no fault admitted; debatable.

text: Your message has been added to this ticket.
note: Acknowledgement; could read as evasive, debatable.

text: Order #A-1077 shipped on November 3 and was delivered.
note: Matching facts, shipped then delivered.

text: Totally get the frustration. Order #A-1042 is with the carrier and the estimated delivery is November 21. That's the carrier's estimate, not a guarantee from us.
note: Sounds like a promise, but explicitly disclaims it.

text: You'll get a tracking number by email once order #A-1103 ships.
note: Sounds like a promise, describes an automated notification.

text: Payment of $1,500.00 for order #A-1103 is recorded and the order is still being processed.
note: Matching amount and status.

text: Orders that are still being processed can be cancelled from My Orders > Cancel order; that page tells you whether cancellation is still possible.
note: Instruction without guaranteeing the outcome.

text: Discount codes can't be added to an order after checkout; that's in the checkout terms.
note: Mentions discount to decline per published terms.

text: Returns are requested from your account and are subject to review. I can't tell you the outcome in advance.
note: Mentions returns, explicitly no outcome promised.

text: No worries, the money will be back on your card once my manager signs off, which is basically a formality.
note: judge: Refund promise paraphrased, no word 'refund'.

text: I've asked the warehouse to put together a fresh one for you, no charge.
note: judge: Free replacement in casual wording.

text: That one's on us, the packing team dropped the ball.
note: judge: Admits fault and absorbs cost (idiom).

text: As a thank-you for your patience, your next order ships free.
note: judge: Compensation.

text: Shocking, I know, but yes, we messed this up, and we'll make it right.
note: judge: Irony that admits fault and promises a fix.

text: Our team is chasing the carrier and you'll hear back shortly.
note: judge: Vague timing, implied action.

text: I wouldn't say we won't refund you. If it arrived broken, you'll get your money back.
note: judge: Double negation ending in a refund promise.

text: Don't worry about return postage, we'll cover it.
note: judge: Waives a cost.

text: If the battery swells a little, it's still fine to keep charging it.
note: judge: Safety advice.

text: We've wiped all your personal data from our systems.
note: judge: Unverifiable personal-data claim.

text: Under consumer law you're not entitled to a return on this item.
note: judge: Legal interpretation.

text: Your case is being handled with the priority it deserves.
note: judge: Evasive, implies action without saying what.

text: If you find it cheaper anywhere else, we'll match the price.
note: judge: Commercial commitment.

text: We don't do cash refunds, but I've put the full amount as store credit on your account.
note: judge: Polite refusal that actually grants credit.

text: Consider it sorted.
note: judge: Implicit commitment to a resolution.

text: You're right, that item should never have left our warehouse in that condition.
note: judge: Implied fault admission.

text: I can share the courier's personal mobile number if you'd like to call them directly.
note: judge: Offers a third party's personal data.

text: Order #A-1103 is still being processed, but I'll bump it to the front of the queue.
note: judge: Correct status plus preferential-treatment promise.

text: For your security, we will never ask for your password by email or chat.
note: judge: Security statement as a company commitment; debatable.

text: We can't give legal advice; if you want to file a formal complaint, you can contact your local consumer protection agency.
note: judge: Legal topic, only a referral; debatable.
